_: A registered hook answers a faulty edit and passes a clean one. This says which edit is which. `check_hooks` runs
the pair against the command `.claude/settings.json` registers. A hook that answers neither reads as silent. A
hook that answers both cannot tell a faulty edit from a clean one.
A hook takes a list of pairs. `probes` names what the pair puts the fault in. A hook reading a comment and a
string literal gets a pair apiece. An arm no pair fires against goes untried.
The pairs live in JSON. A Python module of `generator/` holding their faults would fail `check_prose`.
`TREE` in a path names the root of the repository.
A pair with a `file` fires as an edit into that text. `check_hooks` writes the text under a scratch directory, at
the pair's path from the root of the tree. The payload is then the Edit the tool would send.

prose_answer.py.probes: a rewrite the critic hands back
prose_answer.py._: The critic answers with a verdict per key. A `rewritten` verdict holds its changes under `changes`. `.claude/hooks/prose_answer.py` hands the prose those changes leave to `apply_prose.draft_refusals`.

prose_answer.py.probes: a change citing a rule the conventions do not hold
prose_answer.py._: A change cites a bullet of `.claude/conventions.md` by name, and `prose_answer` refuses a change citing a name that file does not hold. `gate.conventions` holds the names that file writes.

prose_answer.py.probes: a change quoting text the fragment does not hold
prose_answer.py._: A change copies `old` out of the batch character for character. A quote the fragment does not hold names no area to rewrite. `prose_answer` refuses such a change.
